i've: I’ve tried to believe in something external, something that might envelop this and carry it beyond—that’s what we demand of our faiths, isn’t it?

But not ungentle when the aged poor
Pick sticks at hedge-sides; nay, I’ve heard him say,
‘The old dame has a twinge because she stoops:
Well, well, I've told you everything I know--though perhaps I'd have better held my tongue, for little good comes of digging up the past."
He was aware of smiling at her vaguely, and she added, as if condescending to his natural shyness: "I've never seen May looking lovelier.
I’ve seen it tagging on behind her, up streets where chestnut trees flowered, where dusty asphalt had been freshly sprinkled with clean water.

'If bread's the staff of life, they must walk without a staff.'
'While I've a loaf they're welcome to my blessing and the chaff.'
